slides.title: Solar + heliospheric + magnetospheric plasmas
slides.body:
**Solar interior + atmosphere**:
- **Core** ~1.5×10⁷ K, ρ ~ 150 g/cm³ — pp + CNO fusion (Bethe + Weizsäcker 1939; Bethe Nobel 1967).
- **Radiative zone**: photon diffusion ~10⁵ yr to reach convection zone.
- **Convection zone** (outer ~30%): turbulent convection drives **solar dynamo** (α-Ω + Babcock-Leighton) → 22-yr magnetic cycle, sunspots, butterfly diagram.
- **Photosphere**: ~5800 K, optical depth = 2/3; granulation from convection cells.
- **Chromosphere + transition region**: T jumps 10⁴ → 10⁶ K in ~100 km — the **coronal heating problem** (50+ year mystery): why is corona much hotter than photosphere? Candidates: **Alfvén-wave heating** (Schwarzschild 1948; revisited Parker, Cranmer), **nanoflares** (Parker 1988 — many small reconnection events), wave-mode conversion, MHD turbulence cascade. **Parker Solar Probe (2018+)** + **Solar Orbiter (2020+)** now sampling corona directly.
- **Corona**: 10⁶-10⁷ K diffuse plasma; visible at total eclipses; emits X-rays + EUV — basis of SDO + Hinode imaging.

**Solar wind** (Eugene Parker **1958** theoretical prediction; confirmed Mariner 2 1962):
- Continuous outflow ~400-800 km/s, n ~ 5-10 cm⁻³ at 1 AU.
- **Parker spiral** — IMF dragged into Archimedean spiral by solar rotation.
- Slow + fast streams from coronal holes; SIRs/CIRs at stream interfaces.
- **Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs)**: explosive ejections of ~10¹²-10¹³ kg, 100-3000 km/s; drive **space weather** + geomagnetic storms.
- **Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs)**: MeV-GeV ions from CME shocks + flares.

**Earth's magnetosphere** (Chapman + Ferraro 1931 magnetopause; Van Allen 1958 belts):
- Bow shock (collisionless) → magnetosheath → magnetopause (Chapman-Ferraro current).
- **Tail** stretched anti-sunward by solar wind; reconnects in tail center plane.
- **Plasmasphere, ring current, radiation belts, plasma sheet, lobes**.
- **Substorms**: tail reconnection → fast plasma jets earthward → auroral expansion → ring-current injection. Triggered by Earthward IMF B_z reversal + tail loading.
- **Geomagnetic storms** (Dst index): CME impact → ring-current intensification → surface field decrease; aurora seen at low latitudes; satellite damage; GIC in power grids. **Carrington event 1859** = largest known, ~$1-10T cost if today.

**Magnetic reconnection** — central organizing process:
- **Sweet-Parker** (Peter Sweet 1957; Eugene Parker 1957): laminar X-point; rate ~ 1/√S where S = Lundquist number ≈ μ₀ L v_A / η; S ~ 10¹³ in solar corona → way too slow.
- **Petschek 1964**: X-point + slow shocks → rate ~ 0.1 v_A, ~ S^{-1/3}; faster but unstable.
- **Collisionless Hall reconnection**: ion-electron decoupling at ion skin depth d_i = c/ω_pi → rate ~ 0.1 v_A independent of S. **Birn et al. GEM Challenge 2001**.
- **Plasmoid instability** (Loureiro et al. 2007): thin current sheets fragment into plasmoids → fast reconnection.
- **MMS (Magnetospheric Multiscale, NASA 2015–)**: 4 spacecraft in tetrahedral formation, sub-electron-skin-depth resolution — first observations of **electron diffusion region** + verified Hall reconnection physics.

slides.title: Accretion + jets + cosmic ray + extreme plasmas
slides.body:
**Accretion disks**: matter spirals onto compact object (star, black hole, neutron star) losing gravitational PE → radiation. Critical question: **how is angular momentum transported outward**? Laminar viscosity is far too slow.

**Magnetorotational Instability (MRI)** — Steven Balbus + John Hawley **1991 ApJ** (landmark paper): differentially-rotating magnetized fluid is **linearly unstable** when (dΩ/dr) < 0 (Keplerian: Ω ∝ r⁻³/²). MRI grows on local orbital timescale → MHD turbulence → effective viscosity ν ~ α c_s H (Shakura-Sunyaev 1973 α-disk model). **Universal mechanism** for accretion: AGN, X-ray binaries, protoplanetary disks, tidal disruption events.
- Velikhov 1959 + Chandrasekhar 1960 noted the instability for plasmas; Balbus-Hawley applied to disks + showed dominance.
- Confirmed in laboratory: **PROMISE liquid-sodium experiment** (Stefani et al. 2006).
- Modern simulations (Athena, FLASH, PLUTO, idefix) resolve MRI turbulence + jet launching.

**Relativistic jets**:
- **AGN** (Active Galactic Nuclei): supermassive BH (10⁶-10¹⁰ M_sun) accreting → relativistic jets at Lorentz factors Γ ~ 10-50; collimated → pc-scale → Mpc lobes (Cygnus A, 3C 273). **Blandford-Znajek 1977**: BH spin extracts energy electromagnetically → jet power; **Blandford-Payne 1982**: magnetocentrifugal jet launching from disk. **EHT 2019 + 2022**: imaged M87* + Sgr A* photon rings — confirmed Kerr BH + jet base structure.
- **Microquasars**: stellar-mass BH X-ray binaries with jets (SS 433, GRS 1915+105).
- **Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs)**: collapsar (long, > 2 s) + neutron-star merger (short, < 2 s, GW170817 multimessenger 2017). Ultra-relativistic Γ ~ 100-1000 jets; internal + external shocks.
- **Pulsar wind nebulae**: spin-down powered relativistic e⁻e⁺ wind terminates at shock; Crab Nebula = textbook example.
- **Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs)**: ms-duration cosmological transients; magnetar magnetospheric or external-shock origin (Lorimer + Bailes 2007 discovery; Chime 2017+).

**Cosmic-ray acceleration**:
- **First-order Fermi acceleration at shocks** (Krymsky 1977, Bell 1978, Blandford-Ostriker 1978): particles scatter back + forth across shock front, gaining ΔE/E ~ v_shock/c per cycle → power-law spectrum dN/dE ∝ E⁻²·²⁻². Most plausible origin of Galactic cosmic rays up to ~10¹⁵ eV ('knee') in **supernova remnant shocks**.
- **Extragalactic cosmic rays** at E > 10¹⁸ eV ('ankle') — likely AGN, GRBs.
- **GZK cutoff** at ~5×10¹⁹ eV from proton-CMB pion production.
- **Pierre Auger + IceCube + Telescope Array** observe ultra-high-energy cosmic rays + neutrinos.
- **Diffusive shock acceleration (DSA)** simulations + nonlinear back-reaction (Bell instability, magnetic-field amplification).

**Extreme plasmas**:
- **Pair plasmas (e⁻e⁺)**: pulsar magnetospheres, fireballs in GRBs. Symmetric particle content → no charge separation but rich dynamics.
- **Quark-gluon plasma (QGP)**: heavy-ion collisions at RHIC + LHC; perfect-fluid behavior (η/s near KSS bound 1/4π); deconfined quarks + gluons; **strongly-coupled plasma physics meets QCD**.
- **Warm dense matter (WDM)**: Γ ~ 1 strongly-coupled regime; ICF compressed fuel, planetary interiors (Jupiter, Saturn, white dwarfs).
- **Pair-creation cascades** in extreme fields (Schwinger limit 1.3×10¹⁸ V/m); ELI-NP, Apollon, Vulcan PW lasers approaching.

slides.title: Low-temperature + industrial + emerging plasmas
slides.body:
Far more plasma applications by economic value are **low-temperature** (~eV electron energies, ions near room T) than fusion.

**Semiconductor manufacturing — plasma etching + deposition**:
- **Reactive Ion Etching (RIE)**, **Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP)**, **Capacitively Coupled Plasma (CCP)** sources etch nm-scale features in Si, dielectrics, metals.
- **EUV lithography at 13.5 nm** (ASML): laser-produced tin-droplet plasma generates EUV photons — enabled 5 nm + 3 nm + 2 nm logic nodes. Each ASML EUV system = ~$200M; ~600 plasma pulses/sec.
- **Plasma-Enhanced CVD (PECVD)**, ALD: thin-film deposition.
- **Plasma cleaning**, surface treatment, descum.
- Global semiconductor industry = ~$600B/year; plasma processing is the backbone — plasma physics in **every chip** in every phone, laptop, GPU.

**Lighting + displays**:
- **Fluorescent lamps**: low-pressure Hg-Ar discharge emits UV → phosphor → visible. Being replaced by LEDs but historically dominant.
- **High-Intensity Discharge (HID)**: streetlamps, automotive (Xe, Na, Hg).
- **Plasma displays** (PDP TVs, late 1990s-2010s, now obsolete vs OLED/LCD).
- **Neon signs, flat-panel backlights** (CCFLs).

**Electric propulsion — Hall thrusters + ion engines**:
- **Hall-effect thrusters (HET)**: E × B confines electrons, accelerates ions axially. Isp ~ 1500-3000 s, thrust ~ 10s-100s mN. Dominant for **Starlink** (millions of HET-equipped satellites), commsats, deep-space (Dawn, BepiColombo).
- **Gridded ion thrusters** (NSTAR, NEXT, RIT): Isp 3000-5000 s.
- **Magnetoplasmadynamic (MPD), VASIMR (Chang Díaz), pulsed plasma**: higher-power, advanced concepts.
- **Pulsed plasma thrusters (PPTs)**: CubeSats.
- Electric propulsion underpins ~50% of new satellite mass + all economically-viable deep-space missions.

**Plasma medicine**:
- **Cold Atmospheric Plasma (CAP)**: ~1 atm air discharge near room T but with reactive species (RNS/ROS, O, OH, NO, ozone) + UV + E-field.
- **Wound healing**, antimicrobial sterilization (MRSA, hospital infections), dental, blood coagulation.
- **Cancer treatment** — selective apoptosis of tumor cells in vitro + early trials.
- **Plasma-activated water/media** for agriculture + food safety.
- **Tan, Friedman, von Woedtke** — active research groups.

**Industrial + emerging applications**:
- **Arc welding** + plasma cutting + thermal spray (~$15B market).
- **Plasma agriculture**: seed treatment, soil decontamination, plasma-activated nitrogen fixation (alternative to Haber-Bosch).
- **Plasma chemistry**: CO₂ reduction to fuels (e-fuels), ammonia synthesis, hydrogen generation, ozone production.
- **Pollution remediation**: VOCs, flue-gas SOₓ/NOₓ destruction.
- **Plasma 3D printing** + materials synthesis (nanopowders, graphene, nanotubes).

**Private fusion landscape** (2020+ boom):
- **Magnetic confinement**: CFS/SPARC (HTS tokamak); Tokamak Energy (ST40 spherical); Type One Energy + Renaissance + Proxima (stellarator); TAE Technologies (FRC + advanced fuels p-B11); Helion Energy (Polaris, FRC + direct conversion D-³He, Microsoft PPA 2028 target); Zap Energy (sheared-flow Z-pinch); General Fusion (MIF piston-driven liquid metal).
- **Inertial / hybrid**: Focused Energy, Marvel Fusion, Xcimer, Longview, HB11, First Light, Pacific Fusion, Avalanche.
- **~$7B+ private capital since 2020** (FIA tracking); >40 companies; supported by 2022 NIF ignition + JET 59 MJ + HTS breakthrough + climate urgency.

question.question: Magnetorotational instability (MRI): why does B destabilize a Keplerian disk?
question.goal: Sketch the MRI mechanism + identify when the disk becomes turbulent vs laminar.

steps.prompt: Two fluid parcels at slightly different radii in a Keplerian disk are connected by a weak vertical B-field 'spring'. Inner parcel moves faster (Ω ∝ r⁻³/²). What happens?

acceptedAnswers: inner parcel pulls ahead; spring stretches; tension transfers angular momentum outward + inward

steps.reveal: Inner parcel pulls ahead azimuthally → magnetic spring stretches → tension force pulls inner parcel **backward** (loses angular momentum) + outer parcel **forward** (gains).

steps.prompt: Inner parcel loses L (angular momentum) → what happens to its orbit?

acceptedAnswers: moves inward to a lower orbit; outer parcel moves outward

steps.reveal: Lower L → smaller orbital radius → inner parcel moves further in (away from outer); outer parcel gains L → moves further out. **Separation grows** → magnetic spring stretches more → tension grows → runaway. **This is the MRI**: linear instability with growth rate ~ Ω.

steps.prompt: What's the field-strength + wavelength condition for instability?

acceptedAnswers: v_A k < Ω; field weak enough that magnetic tension doesn't overstabilize

hints: If B too strong, magnetic tension stabilizes.
steps.reveal: MRI is unstable when **k v_A < Ω** (i.e. when magnetic tension doesn't dominate). For too-strong B (k v_A > Ω), tension overstabilizes. For zero B, no MRI! **The instability requires a magnetic field but is weakened by too much field** — counterintuitive. Disks self-regulate to MRI-saturated state.

acceptedAnswers: MRI turbulence saturates; effective α ~ 0.01-0.1 in Shakura-Sunyaev ν = α c_s H

hints: Turbulent stress drives outward L transport.
steps.reveal: MRI saturates as **MHD turbulence**; Reynolds + Maxwell stresses transport angular momentum outward → **effective viscosity ν_eff = α c_s H** (Shakura-Sunyaev 1973). Simulations + theory give **α ~ 0.01-0.1**, consistent with observed accretion rates of AGN, X-ray binaries, protoplanetary disks. Resolved discovery of Balbus + Hawley (1991 ApJ) — fundamental to all of accretion physics.

question.question: Why is plasma physics central to astrophysics + many of the most consequential industrial technologies?
options: Plasma is **~99% of baryonic matter** in the visible universe → astrophysics ≡ plasma physics in many guises. Stellar interiors + atmospheres (Saha equation, coronal heating, dynamos), solar wind (Parker spiral, Parker Solar Probe), magnetospheres + space weather (Carrington-class events $T trillion risk), accretion disks (MRI, Balbus-Hawley 1991 → AGN, X-ray binaries, protoplanetary), relativistic jets (Blandford-Znajek/Payne; EHT M87 + Sgr A*), cosmic-ray acceleration at supernova-remnant shocks (Fermi-Bell), GRBs + magnetars + FRBs, pair plasmas + QGP. **Industrially**: every semiconductor (ASML EUV lithography + plasma etch/deposition for every chip in every device; $600B/yr industry); electric propulsion (Hall thrusters in Starlink + most modern satellites + deep space); plasma medicine (cold atmospheric plasma); arc welding; HID + fluorescent lighting; fusion energy (ITER, SPARC, NIF, $7B+ private). Plasma is the **substrate of cosmic + technological civilization** — yet often invisible because the relevant physics requires the Vlasov + MHD machinery developed in this course.
question.explanation: Plasma is ~99% baryonic matter in the universe → astrophysics is largely plasma physics (stars, accretion, jets, cosmic rays, magnetospheres, GRBs, pulsars). Industrially, semiconductors (plasma etch + EUV lithography), electric propulsion (Starlink Hall thrusters), plasma medicine, lighting, welding, fusion — all rely on plasma physics. Cosmic + technological substrate.

question.prompt: A Carrington-class CME (1859 magnitude, Dst ~ -1700 nT) hits Earth tomorrow. Walk through (a) CME propagation 1-3 days from Sun → bow shock impact, (b) magnetopause compression → reconnection rate vs IMF B_z south, (c) ring-current intensification + Dst drop, (d) GIC currents in long power lines + transformer saturation, (e) satellite anomalies + drag enhancement + LEO orbital decay, (f) global cost estimates ($1-10T) + mitigation (transformer hardening, spacecraft sheltering, NOAA SWPC operations + DSCOVR/L1 monitoring).

question.hint: Wavenumber × Alfvén speed less than orbital frequency.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why plasma physics spans both extreme astrophysics + everyday industrial technology + what unifies the two regimes.
question.rubric: Mentions: plasma = ~99% baryonic universe; same Vlasov + MHD equations describe both. Astrophysical: solar/heliospheric (Parker wind, CMEs), magnetospheric (Van Allen, MMS reconnection), stellar coronae (heating problem, Alfvén waves vs nanoflares), accretion disks (MRI, Balbus-Hawley 1991 → angular momentum transport), relativistic jets (AGN/microquasar/GRB; Blandford-Znajek/Payne), cosmic-ray acceleration (first-order Fermi at SNR shocks; Bell 1978), pulsar wind nebulae, FRBs, magnetars, GRBs (multimessenger GW170817), QGP at RHIC/LHC, pair plasmas. Industrial: every semiconductor (plasma etch/deposition + EUV lithography ~$600B), electric propulsion (Hall thrusters on Starlink), plasma medicine, lighting, arc welding, fusion ($7B+ private); HTS revolution + NIF ignition + JET 59 MJ + private fusion all happening in 2020s. Concludes: unified by collective behavior of charged particles + EM fields — same physics, different parameter ranges; the most-applied + least-recognized state of matter, bridging extreme cosmology to your phone.
